scope: Page264 review tabs, tiszafa before-after, Nordmann carousel and four FAQ disclosures.

browser_policy.required: interaction-capable browser with one source and one target tab

static_runtime_reconciliation.before_after_implementation: One-time .js-ba initialization; native range input updates --ba-pos to value + '%'; initial apply runs immediately.
carousel_implementation: translateX by -index*100%; aria-hidden on slides; aria-current on active dot; counter/caption update.
4000 ms setInterval autoplay unless manual, reduced-motion, disconnected or fewer than two slides.
Every byUser navigation path sets manual=true; later start() calls refuse to restart autoplay while manual remains true.
mouseenter/focusin call stop(); mouseleave/focusout call start().
prefers-reduced-motion change calls start(), whose first action stops the current timer and then conditionally restarts.
Broken slides are removed and remaining dot data-go values are reindexed.
static_runtime_reconciliation.manual_latch_contract: Prev/next button, dot navigation, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and qualifying pointer swipe call go(..., true), setting manual=true. Therefore normal source-runtime autoplay is expected to remain stopped after the first manual navigation for that initialized carousel instance, even if hover/focus later exits or reduced-motion preference changes.
static_runtime_reconciliation.important_compound_state_caveat: Hover and focus pause are not represented by independent state flags. Because mouseleave and focusout each call start() unconditionally, autoplay may restart while the other pause condition still remains true before any manual navigation. This is not declared a parity defect until synchronized source behavior is observed; it is an explicit live acceptance edge case.
static_runtime_reconciliation.historical_carousel_role_caveat: oldtrees-runtime-live-qa-v002 sampled source current slide role=group at 2/6 and target role=listItem at 1/6. Later direct v005 proof closed control-name parity but did not re-measure synchronized slide roles. The old unsynchronized role snapshot is therefore neither PASS nor write authority.
static_runtime_reconciliation.faq_note: The common source-interactions-v001.js does not own FAQ disclosure behavior. FAQ must therefore be tested against the current rendered/native/addon disclosure owner before any runtime change is considered.

preconditions: Fresh target tab is page264 and source tab is the exact reference page.
Page264 saved-data hash/JSON is reconciled before attributing a failure to runtime code.
Review static AX still exposes exactly three real tabs plus source-equivalent previous/next, with numbered source dots absent from AX/focus on page264.
Tiszafa remains native range min=0 max=100 step=1 value=50 with data-af-ba-init=1.
Nordmann static controls still match source previous/next plus dots 1-6.
FAQ still contains the four accepted source questions/answers, including Vállalja a munkát akkor is, ha nem én ültettem a növényt?.

tests: Tab1 ArrowRight -> Tab2 -> Tab3 -> Tab1 wrap.
ArrowDown mirrors ArrowRight and ArrowUp mirrors ArrowLeft if current ID14 remains the owner.
Home from Tab2 -> Tab1; End -> Tab3.
Previous/next controls keep selected real tab/panel synchronized.
After every change numbered .af-review-source-dot elements remain tabindex=-1 and aria-hidden=true and do not re-enter focus/AX.
No duplicate tablist/review accessible names appear after dynamic state changes.
review_tabs.failure_policy: Read current ID14 and ID33 owners first. Never add a second review handler from page264 scope.

tests: Native Home/End behavior may be used if source-equivalent; do not add custom key handlers merely for test convenience.
Pointer drag to a clearly different position keeps native value and visual split synchronized.
Return to 50 and confirm accessible naming/alt text remains unchanged.
tiszafa_before_after.failure_policy: Prove missing/duplicate owner or CSS-variable loss before any runtime change; never replace the native range by default.

synchronized_static_ax_gate: Before timing tests, use the source and target first-dot control to put both carousels on slide 1/6, then pause motion by hover/focus or reduced-motion without changing content.
Capture the carousel root/current-slide/noncurrent-slide accessibility roles and names in that same synchronized state.
Require source/target current slide role semantics to match after synchronization; compare aria-hidden/current exposure for all noncurrent slides.
Enumerate the six visible/accessible slide captions and image alt texts in DOM order where obtainable; compare order rather than whichever slide happened to be current before synchronization.

If source remains role=group and target role=listItem in a truly synchronized state, classify a semantic delta and identify the exact current DOM/runtime owner before any change. Do not infer a fix from the historical unsynchronized snapshot.
normal_motion_tests: On a fresh page load with no manual action, no hover and no focus, after >4.1s exactly one forward autoplay advance; another >4.1s gives exactly one more.
ArrowRight exactly one forward; ArrowLeft exactly one backward.
Horizontal pointer swipe >40px with horizontal dominance gives exactly one direction-appropriate advance.
Movement <40px or vertical-dominant movement produces no slide change.
Before any manual navigation, mouseenter held >4.1s pauses autoplay; mouseleave resumes when focus is not inside.
Before any manual navigation, focus held inside >4.1s pauses autoplay; focusout resumes when pointer is not hovering.
manual_latch_tests: Reload/reset both source and target to a fresh carousel instance. After confirming autoplay works once, activate one manual navigation path (prev/next, a dot, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight or qualifying swipe).

After that manual navigation, remove hover/focus and observe >8.2s. Source and target must remain on the manually selected slide unless the live reference proves a different runtime than the recovered source-interactions contract.
After manual=true is established, toggling hover/focus in and out must not create a new autoplay timer.
After manual=true is established, toggling prefers-reduced-motion off/on/off must not restart autoplay through start().
Repeat with at least one pointer path and one keyboard/button path so the byUser latch is not only proven for a single control type.
If target resumes autoplay after manual navigation while source remains latched, inspect the deployed runtime owner/duplicate timer before changing CSS or markup.
compound_pause_state_tests: Run these on a fresh instance before any manual navigation has set manual=true.

Focus a carousel control, then also hover the carousel. Keep focus inside and move pointer out. Observe >4.1s: reference and target must behave the same; specifically record whether autoplay remains paused or restarts.
Hover the carousel, then focus a carousel control. Keep pointer hovering and move focus outside. Observe >4.1s: reference and target must behave the same.
With both hover and focus active, remove both in opposite orders and require no duplicate timers or double-step autoplay.
Do not treat a logically surprising result as a target bug if the source runtime/reference exhibits the same observable behavior; parity outranks redesign.
reduced_motion_tests: On a fresh instance before manual navigation, with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, observe >8.2s with no autoplay advance.
Manual ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and pointer controls remain functional under reduced motion and then establish the same manual latch.
Live media-query toggle, if supported, re-evaluates autoplay without duplicate timers; after manual latch it must not restart autoplay.
nordmann_carousel.failure_policy: Inspect current deployed runtime owner and initialization marker before changing JavaScript or slide semantics. Missing action tooling is not an implementation failure.

tests: Enumerate the four source and four target disclosure controls by exact question text before interacting; do not rely on ordinal position alone.
Record initial expanded/collapsed state for each source and target item and require source-equivalent state.
Activate each disclosure by its native control with pointer/click and require exactly its associated answer to change visibility/expanded state.
Repeat activation by keyboard using the native control's supported Enter/Space semantics; focus must remain on or return predictably to the same question control.

After opening one item, observe whether the source allows multiple simultaneous open items or behaves like an accordion; require the target to match the source rather than imposing a generic accordion rule.
Open/close every item at least once and require no duplicate IDs, duplicate accessible names, orphaned answer region or focus jump outside the FAQ section.
Recheck the restored fourth question after interaction so it cannot silently disappear from the disclosure owner.
faq_disclosures.failure_policy: Identify the current native/addon disclosure owner and exact DOM/ARIA state first. Do not add a second FAQ JavaScript owner merely because generic browser action tooling was previously unavailable.

cross_component_invariants: No test changes visible copy, page264 Elementor data, form state or v004/v005/v006/v007 visual ownership.
No duplicate MutationObserver, timer, keyboard, pointer or disclosure handler is introduced as a workaround.
No form submission, upload, SMTP or external delivery occurs.
Keep only the active source/target pair; do not leave extra autoplay tabs running.
pass_definition: Source and target complete the same observable review, range, carousel and FAQ behavior including synchronized carousel AX semantics, first-manual-action autoplay latch, compound hover/focus, disclosure and reduced-motion states, without AX/focus or visual regression.
